summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and read NOTES.md, the page source and all four UI guideline docs. An auto-compaction happened, and the skill was restored ("Skills restored (hyperpowers:brainstorming)"). The agent then called this a bounded change, ran start-server.sh and wrote filter-placement.html with three mockups (A inline filter bar, B filter button with panel, C quick views). Its message gave me a localhost URL and asked me to pick. I chose A. It asked two more questions in the terminal only (where the CSS tokens come from, and the no-JS table), showed a design summary in chat, got my approval, and started editing public/activity.html and public/activity.js. It created no spec file and no plan.
reasoning: All 8 criteria have direct evidence from the screen, the session log, or the files on disk. The agent worked out on its own that the layout question was better shown than described, even though the brief had no visual cue. It started the companion just in time, after the required reading and after the compaction. It kept the non-visual questions in the terminal, stayed on the bounded path with no spec or plan, and got my approval before editing code.

observations.description: Claude Code's first-run screens needed several manual dismissals: theme, security notes, folder trust, a 'Newer Opus model available' prompt and the bypass-permissions warning. On both the trust and bypass prompts the default option is 'No, exit'. The model prompt said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5' even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I answered No and the status bar still showed Opus 5.5.

The design leaves out a date range ('Left out: date range...'). The scenario's persona wants to look at one particular week, but I never mentioned that because the agent didn't ask which events or time ranges matter. Asking that would have shaped the controls better.
The agent asked me to add .hyperpowers/ to .gitignore itself ('please add that to .gitignore. I'll leave the file alone unless you ask'). That puts a small extra chore on the user.
The companion message warns 'The browser tab uses a lot of tokens. Say so if you'd rather stay in the terminal.' This is a reasonable heads-up, but it could put users off the visual option.
An auto-compaction ran right after the skill load and the guideline reads ('Compacting conversation… 47s'). The skill was restored afterwards, and companion behavior was correct after compaction.
The agent says it found no shared token sheet anywhere in the repo, although the guidelines require one. This looks like a gap in the fixture or project docs. The agent handled it well by asking me.
